questions.stem: A certain sum becomes \(3\) times of itself in \(20\) years at simple interest. In how many years will the same sum become \(2\) times at the same rate?
questions.keySolution:
Given: Sum becomes \(3\) times in \(20\) years
Let principal = \(P\)
Amount after \(20\) years = \(3P\)
SI for \(20\) years = \(3P - P = 2P\)
Rate = \(\frac{SI \times 100}{P \times T} = \frac{2P \times 100}{P \times 20} = 10\%\) per annum
For sum to become \(2\) times:
SI needed = \(2P - P = P\)
Time = \(\frac{SI \times 100}{P \times R} = \frac{P \times 100}{P \times 10} = 10\) years

questions.stem: If a sum of money becomes \(4\) times in \(15\) years at simple interest, what is the rate of interest per annum?
questions.keySolution:
Let principal = \(P\)
Amount = \(4P\)
SI = \(4P - P = 3P\)
Time = \(15\) years
Using formula: Rate = \(\frac{SI \times 100}{P \times T}\)
Rate = \(\frac{3P \times 100}{P \times 15} = \frac{300}{15} = 20\%\) per annum

questions.stem: At \(15\%\) per annum simple interest, a sum becomes \(n\) times in \(20\) years. Find the value of \(n\).

Let principal = \(P\)
SI = \(\frac{P \times 15 \times 20}{100} = 3P\)
Amount = \(P + 3P = 4P\)
Therefore, sum becomes \(4\) times
So, \(n = 4\)
